items.title: 내 주식도 혹시?…수년째 '만년 저평가' 151곳에 저PBR 꼬리표
items.snippet: 장기간 주가순자산비율(PBR)이 낮은 상장사 151곳의 명단이 처음으로 시장에 공개됐다. 이들 기업은 향후 증권사 모바일·홈트레이딩시스템(MTS·HTS)에 '저PBR' 꼬리표가 붙게 돼 자발적인 기업가치 제고에 나서야 한다는 시장의 압박을 받게 될 전망이다.한국거래소는 2일 유가증권시장 96개사, 코스닥시장 55개사 등 총 151개사를 저PBR 기업으로 선정해 공표했다. 이번 조치는 지난 3월 금융당국 등 관계기관이 합동으로 발표한 '자본시장 체질개선 방안'의 핵심 후속 조치다.◇이마트·롯데쇼핑·현대제철도 포함…185곳 중 34곳

items.title: 한국 선박, 홍해 통해 원유 수송…호르무즈 봉쇄 후 20번째
items.snippet: 우리 선박이 홍해를 통해 원유를 수송하고 있다. 호르무즈 해협이 봉쇄된 후 20번째다.해양수산부는 1일 오전 10시 기준 한국 선박이 홍해 얀부항에서 원유를 싣고 수에즈운하를 통과해 국내로 운항 중이라고 밝혔다.해수부는 바브엘만데브 해협이 아닌 북측 수에즈운하를 통과하는 방식이 선사와 화주의 결정으로 이뤄졌다고 말했다.한국 유조선은 지난 4월부터 얀부항에서 원유를 선적하고 남쪽 바브엘만데브 해협을 통해 국내로 운송했으나 사우디아라비아와 친이란 후티 반군의 충돌에 따라 8월 중순부터 수에즈운하를 거치고 있다.hjlee2@yna.co

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 오는 2일 내년도 예산안 시정연설을 한다고 강유정 청와대 수석대변인이 1일 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 당일 정부가 제출한 2027년도 예산안의 편성 방향과 주요 내용을 설명할 예정이다.정부가 국회에 제출한 내년도 예산안은 총지출 기준 820조9000억원으로, 올해 본예산(727조9000억원)보다 12.8% 증가했다. 역대 최대 규모이자 역대 최고 증가율이다.예산안에는 미래 성장동력 확보와 민생 안정, 지방 주도 성장 등을 위한 재정 투자가 담겼다. 특히 162조원 규모의 미래대응기금 신설이 주요 쟁점으로 꼽힌다.이 대통령은 민생 안정과 미래 성장동력 확보를 위한 예산안의 필요성을 강조하고, 국회에 조속한 심의와 처리를 당부할 것으로 예상된다.[서울=뉴시스]

items.title: 靑 “내년초 전작권 성과 기대”… SCM서 ‘전환시점 확정’ 의지

items.title: 민주 “민생 예산 늘려 법정시한내 처리”… 국힘 “포퓰리즘 미래기금 등 134조 삭감”
items.snippet: 국회 예산결산특별위원회가 30일 공청회를 시작으로 820조 원 규모의 내년도 예산안 심사에 본격 돌입했다. 더불어민주당은 민생과 미래 성장동력을 뒷받침할 예산을 적극 확보하겠다는 방침인 반면 국민의힘은 대규모 미래대응기금과 확장재정을 겨냥해 134조 원 수준의 대대적인 삭감을 예고하며 시작부터 맞섰다. 민주당 한병도 원내대표는 이날 최고위원회의에서 “민주당은 민생, 정책, 책임 국감의 기조를 입법과 예산 심사로 이어가겠다”며 “국민을 지키는 예산을 빈틈없이 챙기겠다”고 밝혔다. 박성준 수석대변인도 “민생 성과 극대화에 역량을 집중하겠다”고 했다. 민주당은 예산안을 법정시한 안에 처리하는 데 그치지 않고 일자리·주거·서민금융 등 민생 분야에서 추가 증액도 추진할 방침이다. 정부가 제출한 내년도 예산안은 총지출 820조9000억 원으로 올해보다...

items.title: 반도체 석·박사 대신 취업… 서울대 공대 대학원까지 미달
items.snippet: 반도체 연구 인력을 길러내는 서울대 공대 전기·정보공학부 대학원이 올해 신입생 모집에서 정원을 채우지 못한 것으로 30일 확인됐다. 올해 전기·정보공학부 석·박사 통합 과정 정원은 168명이었는데 입학생은 145명(등록률 86.3%)에 그쳤다. 반도체 호황이 본격화한 지난해에는 정원(165명)을 넘는 169명이 입학했다. 통상 반도체 업황이 좋아지면 관련 대학원에 지원하는 학생도 늘어난다. 하지만 삼성전자·SK하이닉스 등 국내 반도체 기업들이 사상 최대 실적을 낼 올해 오히려 대학원 지원자가 줄었다. 기업은 막대한 이익을 내는데 관련 연구 인력을 길러낼 대학은 비는 ‘호황의 역설’이 나타난 것이다.

items.title: 인천공항서 中항공사 발권 시스템 5시간 오류… 1200명 발 묶여

items.snippet: 법무부가 제주 무사증(무비자)으로 입국한 외국인의 불법 육지 이동을 막기 위해 ‘출도(出島) 사전확인시스템’을 도입한다고 30일 밝혔다. 제주발 국내선 항공권을 발권할 때 외국인 승객이 제주도를 벗어날 수 있는 대상인지 미리 확인하는 시스템이다. 외국인 관광객이 비자 없이 최장 30일간 제주에 머물 수 있는 무사증 제도가 불법 체류, 불법 취업 통로로 악용되고 있다는 본지 보도 에 따른 대책이다. 법무부는 입국 단계 심사도 강화한다. 법무부 관계자는 “무사증 입국 외국인에 대해 입국 목적과 체류 계획 등을 더욱 면밀히 살펴 불법 취업 목적 등으로 입국하는 부적격 외국인을 사전에 차단하겠다”고 했다. 법무부는 올 1월부터 9월까지 항공기 탑승자 사전확인시스템을 통해 인터폴 수배자, 국내 범죄 전력자 등 부적격 외국인 3103명의 입국을 막았다고...

items.title: 박원순 피해자 정보 유출… 후배 女변호사 강제 추행 정철승, 2심서 법정 구속
items.snippet: 서울고법 형사4-2부(재판장 성지용)는 30일 고(故) 박원순 전 서울시장 성추행 사건 피해자의 신상 정보를 공개하고, 술자리에서 후배 여성 변호사를 강제 추행한 혐의로 기소된 정철승 변호사에게 징역 1년 6개월을 선고하고 법정 구속했다. 정씨는 앞서 두 사건으로 1심에서 각각 징역 1년을 선고받았으나 불구속 상태로 2심 재판을 받아 왔다. 재판부는 정씨가 2021년 8월 박 전 시장 유족을 대리하면서 알게 된 성추행 사건 피해자의 개인 정보를 페이스북에 올린 혐의(성폭력처벌법 위반 등)에 대해 1심과 같이 유죄로 판단했다. 재판부는 “신원이 특정될 수 있는 내용이었고, 피해자는 심각한 2차 피해를 입었다”고 했다.

items.title: 내년 장기요양보험료 세대당 月1100원 올라
items.snippet: 내년도 장기요양보험료가 가입 세대당 월평균 1100원 오른다. 보험료율 인상 폭이 2021년도 이후 6년 만에 가장 크다. 장기요양보험은 고령이나 질병 등으로 혼자 일상생활을 하기 어려운 노인에게 방문 요양비나 요양시설 이용비 등을 지원하는 제도로, 이 보험료는 건강보험 가입자 모두가 부과 대상이다. 보건복지부는 30일 장기요양위원회에서 내년도 장기요양보험료율을 올해보다 0.76%포인트 높은 건보료의 13.9%로 결정했다고 밝혔다. 이에 따라 세대당 월평균 장기요양보험료는 1만9029원에서 2만129원으로 오른다. 건보료를 매달 10만원 내는 가입자라면, 장기요양보험료로 1만3900원이 부과되는 것이다.

items.title: 야간버스 모는 아빠 “가족은 내가 돌아갈 종점”
items.snippet: “가족은 버스 기사인 제가 운행을 마치고 돌아가는 종점이자, 내일을 살게 해주는 힘입니다.”(‘31초 영상제’ 최우수상 박용기씨)

items.title: 부산, 아기 울음소리 7년 만에 가장 컸다
items.snippet: 지난 7월 부산에서 태어난 아이는 1365명으로 2019년 7월 이후 가장 많았다. 1년 전보다 144명(11.8%) 늘었다. 올 1~7월 출생아는 9388명으로 지난해 같은 기간보다 15.2% 늘었다. 부산시는 출산·육아 지원을 확대해 이런 증가세를 이어가겠다는 계획이다. 부산시는 올해 추가경정예산을 통해 산후조리비와 산모·신생아 건강관리 서비스 지원 대상을 각각 2000명 늘리기로 했다. 아이 한 명당 산후조리비를 최대 100만원 지원한다. 산후조리원 이용료와 병원 진료비 등으로 쓸 수 있다. 산모·신생아 건강관리 서비스는 전문 교육을 받은 관리사가 출산 가정을 찾아가 산모의 회복을 돕고 신생아를 돌봐주는 제도다.

items.title: “암 환자도 이젠 집에서 치료해야… 환자도 병원도 모두 만족할 수 있어”
items.snippet: “이제 병원들도 재택 의료에 우선순위를 둬야 합니다. 환자는 물론이고, 병원 입장에서도 이를 통해 얻는 것이 많습니다.” 스웨덴 살그렌스카 대학병원의 부부 할베리(Boubou Hallberg) 원장은 지난 20일 본지 인터뷰에서 우리나라가 확대하려는 ‘방문 진료’ 관련 질문이 나오자, 이같이 답했다. 서울에서 열린 국제병원연맹 ‘세계 병원 대회’(20~22일) 참석차 방한한 할베리 원장은 스웨덴 내 최대 규모(약 1600병상에 직원 1만8000명 근무) 병원을 이끌면서도, 방문 진료와 유사한 ‘재택 의료’의 자국 내 확산을 위해 앞장서온 의료인으로 통한다.

items.title: 25년간 매일 ‘아침 편지’… “400만명 지친 마음 보듬었죠”
items.snippet: “400만 명에게 보내는 편지가 아닙니다. 단 한 사람에게 쓴 편지가 매일 아침 그만큼의 집에 도착하는 것입니다.” 지난 20일 충북 충주시 ‘깊은산속 옹달샘’ 집필실에서 만난 고도원(75) 아침편지문화재단 이사장은 25년간 편지를 이어 온 힘을 이렇게 설명했다. 아침편지문화재단은 29일 ‘제13회 21세기 인문가치포럼’ 개막식에서 ‘2026 인문가치대상’ 단체 부문 상을 받았다. 25년간 좋은 글을 무료로 전하고 그 울림을 명상과 나눔으로 확장한 공로다.

items.snippet: 이번 국정감사에서 의료계 최대 이슈는 9월 30일 있었던 아주대 소아응급센터 압수수색. 생후 4개월 아기가 외래진료 중 호흡곤란 등의 증세를 보여 소아응급센터로 옮겨져 응급 처치를 받다가 사망했는데, 이로 인해 해당 병원 의사들이 범죄자 취급을 받은 건 그냥 넘어가서는 안 될 일이 맞다. 하지만 위 사건에 묻혀 조명되지 않은 건이 하나 더 있었으니, 그건 10월 7일 나온, 더불어민주당 송영길 의원의 발언이었다. 그는 국군의무사령관에게 군의관이 감소하고 있는 것에 대한 대책을 묻던 중 다음과 같이 말한다. “군 의사 같은 경우는 전쟁 상황이라는 특수 상황에서 전문의의 고도의 의학지식이 필요한 건 아니잖아요.” 이 말만으로도 납득이 어렵지만, 그가 내놓은 해법은 더 충격이었다. “긴급하게 응급적으로 처리할 수 있는 PA(Physician Ass...

items.snippet: 서울에 사는 디자이너 박모(39·여)씨는 최근 혼자 당일치기로 설악산 등산을 다녀왔다. 등산 버스 모바일 앱에서 5만원대 왕복 차편을 예약했다.

items.title: 한 잔 술에 깃든 그리운 기억들
items.snippet: 서울에 갈 일이 있을 때마다 아버지는 나를 데리고 정릉 큰이모네를 들렀다. 시장에서 장사를 하던 큰이모는 외할머니를 도와 다른 이모들을 자식처럼 키웠다고 했다. 쭈뼛거리며 자리를 잡으면 상냥한 사촌 형수는 나를 반기며 밥상을 차렸고 나보다 훨씬 나이가 많은 사촌 형은 중년이 가진 조금은 피곤한 표정으로 내 손을 잡았다. 아버지는 몇 마디 이야기를 나눈 뒤 큰이모부와 마주 앉았다. 곧 큰이모가 가지고 온 술상에는 막걸리와 반찬 몇 개가 놓여 있었다. 큰이모부와 아버지는 배추김치, 두부, 달걀 프라이 같은 집 반찬만 먹으며 몇 시간이고 양반다리 자세로 앉아 웃고 떠들었다. 나는 밥을 먹고 소파에 앉아 있다가, 그마저도 지치면 빈방 어느 구석에서 굴러다니는 책을 집어 들고 읽으며 시간을 보냈다. 큰이모부가 취해 자겠다고 안방으로 들어가면 그제야 아...

items.title: 노벨상까지 받은 분자 연구, 왜 과학자들은 재앙을 걱정할까
items.snippet: 그리스 신화에서 잘생긴 외모로 유명한 나르키소스는 다른 사람의 말을 메아리처럼 반복하는 요정 에코의 사랑을 거절했다가 자신과 사랑에 빠지는 저주를 받았다. 그는 거울처럼 맑은 샘물에 비친 자신만 바라보다가 죽어 자기도취를 뜻하는 나르시시즘이란 말이 생겼다. 그의 얼굴은 그지없이 아름다웠지만, 거울을 보듯 마주한 자기 모습은 삶의 의지를 빼앗을 뿐이었다.

items.title: 8만원어치 주문, 지출은 0원… 이게 된다고?
items.snippet: 크리스피 반반치킨에 치즈볼 5개, 탕수육(대)과 마라탕, 아이스 아메리카노에 딸기 생크림 케이크까지. 먹고 싶은 음식을 배달앱 장바구니에 담았더니 총 8만2700원어치다. 빠르게 배달해 준다는 ‘토끼배달’을 선택하자 기본 배달비 4000원에 추가금 1000원이 붙었다. 결제 버튼을 누르자 순식간에 매장에서 주문을 확인했다는 알림이 뜨고, 지도 위로 배달원의 위치가 움직이기 시작했다. 잠시 뒤 ‘배달 완료!’라는 안내가 떴다. 영수증에는 ‘이번 주문으로 아낀 금액 8만7700원, 4380kcal 아끼셨어요!!’라는 문구가 적혀 있었다. 하지만 실제로 배달된 음식은 하나도 없었다. 빠져나간 돈도 0원이다. 가짜 배달앱 ‘음식만안와요’에서 주문했기 때문이다.

items.title: “해외에서 엄마 김치 먹고 싶은 분?”… 시골 우체국이 살아남는 법
items.snippet: ‘백수’ 우체국이 새 일자리를 찾았다. 전남광주 영광군 백수읍에 있는 우체국 이야기다. 이 우체국은 인구 감소로 우편물이 줄어 새로운 활로가 절실한 상황이었다. 눈을 해외로 돌렸다. 김장철인 지난해 12월, SNS에 ‘엄마 김치가 그리운 해외 교민들의 김치 배송을 돕겠다’는 글을 올렸다. 이른바 ‘김치 해외 배송 대행’이다. 과정은 이렇다. 백수우체국에 신청하면 집으로 김치를 담을 수 있는 금속 용기(캔)를 보내준다. 여기에 김치를 담아 백수우체국으로 보내면 된다. 나머지는 우체국 직원들이 알아서 한다. 김치캔을 보랭 상자에 넣고 산소·발효 가스 흡수제와 보랭 팩 등을 추가해 재포장한 뒤 국제특급우편(EMS)으로 원하는 해외 주소에 발송해 준다. 소비자는 EMS 요금만 내면 된다.

items.title: 헌법 개정 논의, 권력 구조
items.snippet: 헌법은 국가의 근본 조직과 작용을 규정하는 최고 규범으로서, 큰 틀에서 보면 기본권에 관한 조항과 통치 기구에 관한 조항이 그 핵심적 내용입니다. 그런데 헌법에 규정된 통치 기구 내지 권력 구조에 관한 조항도 권력 분립과 견제와 균형을 통해 국민의 기본권을 보장하기 위한 장치입니다. 즉 권력 분립을 통해 권력 집중에 의한 독재의 위험을 막아 국민의 기본권을 보장하는 것, 그것이 민주 헌법의 기본 원리입니다. 우리 헌법도 기본적으로 그 내용이나 정신에 있어 다름이 없습니다. 그렇지만 그 정신이 현실 정치에서 완전하게 구현되고 있지 아니한 것은 그 운영상 문제 때문이라고 할 것입니다. 제왕적 대통령이라는 비아냥이 등장하고, 의회 권력이 불합리하게 비대해지고 대화와 타협은 멀어져 입법 독재라는 비난이 가해지고, 미성숙한 정당 정치 모습에 뜻있는 국...

items.title: 빌딩이 불타고 사람이 죽어나간다… 언제 보복당할지 모르는 사회
items.snippet: #1. 지난 20일 서울 역삼동 S빌딩 3층과 인근 H빌딩 4층에서 7분 간격으로 불이 나 시민 26명이 다쳤다. 두 건물은 직선거리로 200m 떨어져 있다. 경찰은 이날 오후 지하철 1호선 동묘앞역 인근에서 방화 혐의를 받는 70대 남성 이모씨를 검거했다. 이씨는 특허법인이 허위 특허등록증을 발급하는 등 자신에게 사기를 쳤다고 생각해 불을 질렀다고 경찰에 진술했다. S빌딩 3층과 H빌딩 4층에는 모두 특허법인 사무실이 입주해 있다. 이씨는 2022년에도 이번에 불을 지른 특허법인 사무실을 찾아가 휘발유를 뿌리며 협박한 혐의로 구속돼 징역 2년 6개월을 선고받은 바 있다.

items.title: 오랜만에 옷장서 꺼낸 코트, 퀴퀴한 악취 원인은?
items.snippet: 조향사로서 냄새에 민감하다 보니 이맘때면 유독 신경 쓰이는 냄새가 있다. 옷장 깊숙이 보관했다 꺼낸 코트에서 나는 퀴퀴한 냄새. 곰팡이에 피지, 땀, 나프탈렌까지 뒤섞인 악취다. 정작 옷을 입은 사람은 잘 모를 수 있다. 후각은 반복되는 냄새에 익숙해지기 때문이다. 깨끗하게 보관했다고 생각한 코트에서 왜 악취가 날까? 가장 큰 원인 중 하나는 습기다. 여름철 습기를 머금은 옷을 통풍이 잘되지 않는 옷장에 오래 넣어두면 곰팡이가 자라기 쉬워진다. 곰팡이는 번식하면서 퀴퀴한 냄새를 풍긴다. 여기에 목깃이나 소매에 남아 있던 땀과 피지가 시간이 지나며 미생물에 의해 분해되면서 텁텁한 냄새를 더한다. 겨울옷을 보관할 때 방충제인 나프탈렌을 사용하는 가정이 있다. 이미 곰팡이와 피지 냄새가 밴 코트에 나프탈렌의 강한 냄새까지 겹치면 훨씬 불쾌하게 느껴...

items.title: 분식집에서 사라진 김밥… 파인다이닝 주연으로
items.snippet: 흑백요리사 2에 ‘서울 엄마’로 출연한 우정욱 셰프가 한글과 영어로 된 김밥 요리책 ‘김밥 책’을 최근 냈다. 출판 기념회에는 국내 유일 미쉐린 3스타 레스토랑 ‘밍글스’ 강민구 오너 셰프를 비롯해 국내 정상급 셰프·외식업계 관계자 150여 명이 참석했다. 예상보다 많이 모였다. 우 셰프는 “(자신의 식당) ‘수퍼판’을 찾는 외국 손님들로부터 ‘김밥 마는 법 알려주는 요리책을 내달라’는 요청을 많이 받았다”고 했다.

items.title: 의사가 된 ‘톤즈의 아이’... “이태석 신부의 길 걷습니다”
items.snippet: 2001년, 내전 중이던 아프리카 수단 남부의 한 마을에 폭격이 가해졌다. 당시 열한 살 무렵이던 조셉 볼(36)은 아름드리나무 아래에서 수업을 듣고 있었다. 교사(校舍)가 없어 대신 교실 역할을 하던 나무였다. 그는 “아직도 그날을 기억한다”고 했다. 함께 공부하던 친구 일곱 명이 눈앞에서 목숨을 잃었다. 총탄에 쓰러지는 사람들, 전쟁터로 향하는 또래 소년병들. 그의 눈에 비친 세상은 전쟁이 전부였다. 가족을 지키기 위해 군인이 되겠다고 결심했다. 살아남기 위해 총을 들어야 한다고 믿었다.

items.title: ‘사과나무 옆 미술관’… 샤갈, 요시토모, 론 뮤익, 서도호까지 예술의 향기가 진동했다
말에 실려왔다 걸어서 나간다는, 혼슈 최북단 숨겨진 秘湯을 아십니까?
items.snippet: 혼슈 북단, ‘기타도호쿠(北東北) 3현’으로 불리는 아오모리·이와테·아키타현은 일본의 오지로 불리는 곳이다. 일본인조차 평생 이곳을 밟아보지 못하고 죽는 사람이 적지 않다고 할 만큼 산도 깊고, 물도 깊다. ‘비탕(秘湯)’, ‘탕치(湯治)’란 말도 이곳을 여행하며 처음 들었다. 사람 손길이 거의 닿지 않은 ‘숨겨진 온천’이란 뜻으로, 병이 치유될 만큼 몸에 좋은 성분이 다량으로 함유된 온천이 많다고 했다. ‘일본 온천여행’을 펴낸 박성희 인페인터글로벌 대표는 “기타도호쿠 지역의 명탕(名湯)들은 활화산 수맥에서 솟아나는 자연수로 기준치를 뛰어넘는 유황과 염화물 성분을 품은 것은 물론 용출량이 풍부해 원천수를 여과 없이 욕조로 흘려보내는 ‘가케나가시’ 방식을 유지한다”고 했다.

items.title: 여덟 가지 아름다운 경치를 표현한 산수화
items.snippet: 소상팔경도(瀟湘八景圖)는 중국 동정호(洞庭湖) 주변 소수(瀟水)와 상수(湘水) 유역의 여덟 가지 아름다운 경치를 그린 그림이다. 그 전통의 시작은 중국 북송으로 거슬러 올라간다. 11세기 문인 관료인 송적(宋迪)의 득의작(得意作·작가가 뜻한 바를 잘 구현한 작품)으로 평사낙안(平沙落雁), 원포귀범(遠浦歸帆), 산시청람(山市晴嵐), 강천모설(江天暮雪), 동정추월(洞庭秋月), 소상야우(瀟湘夜雨), 연사모종(煙寺暮鐘), 어촌석조(漁村夕照)가 있고 이를 팔경(八景)이라 했다는 기록이 전한다.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. items.title: When Does Heterogeneity Pay Off? Understanding GPU-WSE System Complementarity
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational comp...

items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. items.title: ZnO/Ni interface-activated enhancement of spintronic terahertz emission from Ni/Pt bilayers
items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with...

items.title: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
items.abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. items.abstract: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. items.abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. items.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
items.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and...

items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. This fixed substrate reduces deployment to a spatial search via Delay-Aware Reservations and Spatial Annealing (DAR...

items.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. We highlight a III-V semiconductor photonic structure operating at 24.5 um, a wavelength with few laser...

items.title: Surface Functionalization with Lasers: from Nanostructures to Applications
items.abstract: Pulsed laser sources stand out as remarkable and versatile tools in the growing interdisciplinary field of materials science, offering capabilities for tailoring and customizing materials to meet specific requirements. Their ability to induce different controlled material alterations allows enhancing material properties that might otherwise remain elusive. In essence, laser-induced material modifications encompass a spectrum of transformative processes, ranging from subtle topographical changes in the nano- and microscale, to intricate chemical modifications. Among the challenges to overcome are the creation of approaches that allow tuning the properties of light to optimize interactions on various types of solids, including metals, semiconductors, and dielectrics. Understanding these interactions is paramount towards efficiency increase of the processing techniques. This chapter embarks...

items.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
items.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

items.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
items.abstract: Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. We derive a closed-form critical response threshold beyond which RIL exceeds the or...

items.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
items.abstract: Rowhammer is a hardware vulnerability in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in which repeated accesses to one or more aggressor rows can induce bit-flips in nearby victim rows. This phenomenon violates a core assumption of conventional programming language semantics: that reading from or writing to one memory location does not modify others. Despite the security importance of this phenomenon, there is no widely established formal framework connecting Rowhammer faults with program behaviour. This makes it difficult to reason rigorously about the efficacy of proposed Rowhammer defences and the program-level guarantees they provide. To address this gap, we present a probabilistic small-step operational semantics for an idealised imperative language subject to Rowhammer-style faults. The semantics is high-level in that it abstracts from DRAM internals and semiconductor physics. A general pr...

items.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
items.abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. The realization of this concept promises to redefine core paradigms in optics and fundamental physics. Because the mi...

items.title: Phonon-Dressed Quasiparticles in Epitaxial Scandium Nitride Resolved by Soft X-ray ARPES
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions govern quasiparticle energies, lifetimes, and temperature-dependent band structures in semiconductors. However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. First-principles spectral-function calculations due to electron-phonon coupling reproduce the measured spectra, capturing a pronounced quasiparticle kink ~2.3 eV below the valence-band maximum, phonon satellite features arising from long-range electron-phonon coupling, and a direct bandgap zero-point renormalization of -124.3 meV within the non-adiabat...

items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. Hydrogen binds cooperatively to the silicon vacancy, which goes directly from bare to fully passivated $V$H$_4$. In c...

items.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the solution of the drift-diffusion equations with...

items.title: Automated Multi-Line Bug Repair Using Model Checker Aided LLMs: A Case Study on RISC-V Processors
items.abstract: Functional verification of Register-Transfer Level(RTL) designs has become a critical bottleneck in modern semiconductor development, often consuming the majority of project resources. Debugging, in particular, remains an especially time-consuming task, requiring careful analysis of simulation traces or counterexamples. Recent work has explored applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to RTL debug and repair with great promise. However, the existing approaches typically are for single-line bugs, operate in open-loop, rely heavily on prompts or retrieval, lack scalability, and often produce incorrect fixes. In this paper, we propose a novel automated RTL bug repair methodology that combines LLMs, assertions, and a model checker to provide scalable, trustworthy semantic grounding and formal guarantees. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. items.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
items.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of $α$-MnTe. items.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
items.abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. items.abstract: Semiconductor triple-quantum dots (TQDs) are a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but the community has so far lacked access to affordable and flexible high-speed control electronics. SpinQICK, an open-source spin qubit-control package built on the Xilinx Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC), directly addresses this gap by leveraging the high sampling-rate signal generation and advanced digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities of the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) to enable precise time-domain voltage control and readout of semiconductor spin qubits. In this paper, we use spinQICK to demonstrate coherent control, state preparation, and readout of a fully connected triangular exchange-only device. We also introduce and experimentally verify a novel dynamical decoupling (DD) sequence enabled by the triangular TQD and leverage its unique decoup...

items.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
items.abstract: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that...

items.title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
items.abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. items.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
items.abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models and spatial resolution. Here we demonstrate a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model that establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit. Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
items.abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. items.title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization
items.abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a gr...

items.title: The Reaction of Financial Markets to the Releases of DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K3: A Critical Analysis
items.abstract: This paper compares financial-market reactions to the releases of DeepSeek R1 in January 2025 and Kimi K3 in July 2026. Both AI models were presented as credible Chinese competitors near the capability frontier, but their releases conveyed different economic information. DeepSeek R1 combined open weights with unusually low reported training and inference costs, prompting investors to reassess expected demand for computing infrastructure and producing large stock-price decreases among semiconductor and data-centre-related firms. Kimi K3 instead entered at broadly frontier prices and generated a market reaction concentrated more heavily among rival Chinese AI laboratories. Drawing on descriptive event-window evidence, model capability and cost comparisons, subsequent industry developments, and the historical diffusion of open-source software, the paper argues that open-weight models redist...

items.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
items.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates addition...

items.title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
items.abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. items.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
items.abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI):...

items.title: Electronic, structural and magnetic properties of goldene nanoribbons
items.abstract: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold. Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Our findings demonstrate that the electronic structure of these nanoribbons depends strongly on both edge chirality and ribbon width. Depending on the boundary configuration, the systems can exhibit semiconducting behavior with electronic band gaps of approximately 0.77 eV and 0.04 eV, or retain metallic characteristics. Additionally, the edge regions act as electronically active site...

items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. items.abstract: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-ato...

items.title: Observation of Size-dependent Optical Modes and Confinement in Fin Cavities using Angle-Resolved Cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. FDTD also reveals a transition from multi-mode to single-longitudinal-mode behavior in 200-nm fins, consistent with experimentally observed fringe narrowing. Increasing fin length...

items.title: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
items.abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. items.title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
items.abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. The results are...

items.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
items.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature depen...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
items.abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI$_2$ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic excito...

items.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to about 50mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. items.title: Coherent Phonon Generation from Prethermal Carrier Populations in a Semiconductor
items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Rather than committing to a single representation, TileCas allows an agent to transfer and refine candidates across levels through Cross-Level Diagnosis, which maps correctness and performance feedback to actionable controls at different abstraction level...

Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification
items.abstract: The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have made rapid inroads into Electronic Design Automation (EDA), approximately 74.6% of existing studies target static Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation, leaving post-simulation verification and interactive waveform debugging largely untouched. We introduce Back-to-the-Future (BTTF), an end-to-end agentic framework that closes this infrastructural gap. BTTF distills massive, unstructured simulation dumps into a normalized relational SQLite database and couples it with a collaborative multi-agent orchestration engine that translates natural-language verification queries into schema-aware SQL while correlating signal anomalies with versioned...

items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: SimSkip: StrongARM-Comparator Similarity Sensing with SAR-Skipping-Aware Training for Analog Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Analog-to-digital conversion dominates the energy and area of analog compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators. This paper presents SimSkip, a successive-approximation-register (SAR) skipping scheme that combines a lightweight StrongARM-comparator similarity detector with SAR-skipping-aware training. When two held voltages are similar, the upper bits of the preceding code are reused to skip SAR comparisons. Detector-induced disturbance extracted from 55-nm CMOS simulations and bit-exact prefix saturation are embedded in the forward pass, and the network learns to tolerate them through quantization-aware training and knowledge distillation. On an ISAAC-based W4A4 WRN-28-10, SimSkip achieves 77.23% CIFAR-100 top-1 accuracy (mean of three seeds) versus 78.4% for the baseline, while reducing SAR comparisons by 48.2% across three hardware-modeled layers. A first-order model estimates a 27.2% net A...

items.title: Accelerating Periodic Coupled Cluster and Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theories With Frozen Natural Orbitals
items.abstract: We present a unified frozen natural orbital (FNO) framework for periodic Gaussian-orbital post-Hartree-Fock calculations with explicit k-point sampling. The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Moller-Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. FNO truncation reproduces canonical results with small errors while substantially reducing computational cost. SS-FNO enables accurate large-basis band-gap calculations, including quadruple-zeta results, w...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amp...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: JANUS: A Multi-modal Foundation Neural Sampler for Disordered Materials
items.abstract: Disordered materials are central to modern technologies, from high-performance alloys to quantum devices, yet understanding and designing them requires exploring an enormous space of compositions and atomic arrangements. Here we introduce JANUS, a multimodal neural sampler that jointly explores chemical composition, atomic structure and volume, learning directly from the energy of the system without requiring pre-generated equilibrium configurations. Across test systems, JANUS reproduces reference equilibrium properties and recovers free energy and phase behavior with about three orders of magnitude fewer energy evaluations than reference Monte Carlo sampling. In multicomponent alloys, JANUS reproduces experimentally observed local chemical order and can be steered to further enhance chemical order and stiffness. Coupled to an evolutionary language model agent, it also enables efficient...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
items.abstract: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. Th...

items.title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess ener...

items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter'').
